entries.hook: The places between land and water protect more than we see. 🌿
entries.summary: World Wetlands Day on 2 February draws attention to marshes, peatlands, lakes, mangroves and other water-shaped ecosystems. These places shelter wildlife, help manage water and support local livelihoods. The observance invites communities to value wetlands as living infrastructure rather than empty land.
entries.origin: In 1971, countries adopted the Convention on Wetlands in Ramsar, Iran, to cooperate on conserving important wetland sites. On 30 August 2021, the UN General Assembly established World Wetlands Day as an official United Nations observance. The convention's 1971 adoption and the day's 2021 proclamation are different historical events.
entries.whyThisDate: 2 February recalls the 1971 signing of the Ramsar Convention, while the official UN observance was proclaimed in 2021.
entries.whyItMatters: Wetlands help regulate water, store carbon and support species as well as people. When they are drained or polluted, those benefits can disappear. Understanding the connection between ecosystems and everyday life makes conservation a practical question, not an abstract slogan.
waysToTakePart: Find an officially protected wetland near your community and read why it matters.
Learn about a local restoration project and how it works with residents and wildlife.

entries.hook: One spark of discovery can illuminate many fields. 💡
entries.summary: The International Day of Light, marked on 16 May, connects scientific discovery with daily life. Light underpins vision, communications, medicine, energy and art. UNESCO uses this day to encourage cooperation and to show how scientific knowledge and creative expression can widen opportunity.
entries.origin: The date recalls Theodore Maiman's first successful operation of a laser on 16 May 1960. UNESCO's General Conference proclaimed the International Day of Light in 2017, following the International Year of Light in 2015. The first annual celebration took place in 2018; none of those dates should be confused with the invention of the laser itself.
entries.whyThisDate: 16 May honours the 1960 laser milestone; UNESCO's proclamation came in 2017 and the first observance in 2018.
entries.whyItMatters: Light-based technologies contribute to diagnostics, fibre-optic communication, efficient energy systems and creative culture. Scientific benefits depend on education and access, so the day also asks who can participate in research and who can benefit from its results.
waysToTakePart: Visit a science museum or public event explaining light and optical technologies.
Explore how lighting accessibility or energy-efficient light can improve a shared space.

entries.hook: Two wheels, many routes to a more accessible city. 🚲
entries.summary: World Bicycle Day celebrates the bicycle as a practical way to move, explore and connect. On 3 June, the United Nations highlights cycling's contribution to sustainable transport, physical activity and social inclusion. The message is not that everyone must cycle, but that safe choices should be available.
entries.origin: On 12 April 2018, the United Nations General Assembly adopted resolution A/RES/72/272, declaring 3 June World Bicycle Day. The resolution recognized the bicycle's affordability, versatility and potential role in sustainable development. Cycling as a human activity is much older than 2018; the year refers specifically to the UN designation.
entries.whyThisDate: The General Assembly designated 3 June in its 2018 resolution; the calendar date is not presented as the bicycle's invention day.
entries.whyItMatters: Well-planned cycling networks can make short trips easier, especially where routes connect to public transit. Safe streets, accessible design and respectful sharing of space matter more than symbolic celebrations, because cycling is useful only when people can choose it safely.
waysToTakePart: Review the safest cycling route to a nearby destination, including traffic and road conditions.
Support a local initiative for accessible bike parking, safe routes or cycling education.

entries.hook: A practice with ancient roots and a modern global day. 🧘
entries.summary: International Day of Yoga is observed on 21 June as an invitation to learn about a practice originating in India. Yoga encompasses traditions of movement, attention and reflection; it is more than a single fitness routine. The United Nations observance acknowledges its international reach while respecting its cultural origins.
entries.origin: India proposed a worldwide day dedicated to yoga during the 69th session of the UN General Assembly. On 11 December 2014, the Assembly adopted resolution 69/131 and designated 21 June as International Day of Yoga. The practice itself developed long before 2014, so its historical roots must not be confused with the founding of this modern observance.
entries.whyThisDate: 21 June was selected in the 2014 UN proclamation; it is not a claim about when yoga originated.
entries.whyItMatters: Learning a practice in context can encourage respect for the culture and people who shaped it. The day also offers a chance to discuss accessible opportunities for movement and reflection without treating yoga as a medical cure or a replacement for qualified care.
waysToTakePart: Read an introduction to yoga's history from a reliable cultural or educational institution.
Try an accessible beginner session with qualified guidance, adapting movements to your needs.

entries.hook: Safe food depends on a chain of careful decisions. 🥗
entries.summary: World Food Safety Day on 7 June shines a light on the work behind food that people can trust. Producers, transporters, shops, kitchens and consumers all affect food safety. The day encourages prevention, reliable information and shared responsibility across the food system.
entries.origin: On 20 December 2018, the United Nations General Assembly adopted resolution 73/250 establishing World Food Safety Day. The first annual celebration took place on 7 June 2019. FAO and WHO jointly facilitate the observance, connecting food safety with human health and sustainable food systems.
entries.whyThisDate: 7 June is the annual date selected by the UN after the 2018 proclamation; celebrations began in 2019.
entries.whyItMatters: Foodborne risks can affect households, public health and trade. Good practice requires cooperation across the supply chain, from handling and storage to inspections and communication. Information that people can verify is more useful than alarming or unsupported claims.
waysToTakePart: Review official local food-storage and preparation advice from a recognized food-safety authority.
Learn how food safety is monitored along one product's journey from producer to consumer.

entries.hook: Understanding tobacco harms is part of public-health literacy. 🚭
entries.summary: World No Tobacco Day, observed on 31 May, is a WHO-led awareness day about tobacco-related harm and prevention. It draws attention to public policy, industry practices and the information people need to make informed decisions. Campaign themes change by year, but the day has a consistent public-health purpose.
entries.origin: WHO Member States created World No Tobacco Day in 1987 through a World Health Assembly resolution, originally calling for a global no-smoking day in April 1988. A subsequent 1988 resolution established 31 May as the recurring observance date. Thus 1987 is the founding year, while the modern calendar arrangement comes from 1988.
entries.whyThisDate: 31 May follows the WHO's 1988 annual scheduling decision; the original establishment was in 1987.
entries.whyItMatters: People benefit from credible health information and from policies that reduce exposure and prevent harm. The day can encourage public discussion without blaming individuals or presenting general awareness content as personalized medical advice.
waysToTakePart: Read the latest World Health Organization materials on tobacco prevention and public-health policy.
Share a trustworthy local resource for people seeking professional support to stop using tobacco.

entries.hook: Behind population numbers are lives, choices and communities. 🌍
entries.summary: World Population Day on 11 July invites reflection on how demographic change intersects with health, education, rights and sustainable development. Population statistics describe societies, but responsible discussion also considers the people and decisions behind those numbers.
entries.origin: Interest grew after the Day of Five Billion, observed on 11 July 1987. In 1989, the UN Development Programme's Governing Council established World Population Day; the first observance took place in 1990. The UN General Assembly subsequently supported its continuation through resolution 45/216. The years 1987, 1989 and 1990 refer to distinct milestones.
entries.whyThisDate: 11 July recalls the 1987 Day of Five Billion; the international observance was established in 1989 and first marked in 1990.
entries.whyItMatters: Demographic change affects planning for schools, housing, care and public services. Figures can inform decisions, but they should be presented with context, respect for rights and attention to local differences rather than used to reduce people to a single statistic.
waysToTakePart: Explore a recent official population dataset and check how it describes uncertainty.
Read about how local planners use demographic evidence to improve essential services.

entries.hook: Every learner's story also includes someone who taught them. 📚
entries.summary: World Teachers' Day on 5 October celebrates teachers and asks what support they need to do their work well. The day highlights the value of education, professional preparation and fair working conditions, alongside the people who help learners grow.
entries.origin: The date commemorates the 1966 ILO/UNESCO Recommendation concerning the Status of Teachers, an international reference on teachers' rights, responsibilities, training and conditions. World Teachers' Day has been celebrated since 1994. The 1966 recommendation and the 1994 annual observance are distinct events.
entries.whyThisDate: 5 October marks the anniversary of the 1966 ILO/UNESCO teachers' recommendation; the worldwide observance began in 1994.
entries.whyItMatters: Teachers' work depends on professional learning, time, resources and supportive school communities. Appreciating an individual teacher is meaningful, while understanding the conditions behind good teaching can prompt longer-lasting improvements for both educators and students.
waysToTakePart: Thank a teacher for a specific lesson or encouragement that made a difference.
Read the UNESCO and ILO guidance on teacher support and discuss one practical improvement.
